root_cause.text: In fs/smb/server/transport_rdma.c, smb_direct_post_send_data() kept treating sendmsg ownership as local after post_sendmsg had moved msg into send_ctx, causing an error path after smb_direct_flush_send_list() to free the same sendmsg a second time.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the comment “From here msg is moved to send_ctx and we should not free it explicitly,” changes the flush failure path from `goto err` to `goto flush_failed`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that `smb_direct_flush_send_list()` already calls `smb_direct_free_sendmsg()`, so calling it again caused the double-free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid freeing a send message after ownership has moved to send_ctx when flush_send_list fails, while still restoring credits.
intent_record.what: A comment was added clarifying that after a certain point the msg object is transferred to send_ctx ownership, and the error path after smb_direct_flush_send_list() was changed from jumping to the err label to a new flush_failed label that skips smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, msg) while still executing the subsequent credit restoration cleanup.
intent_record.how: This prevents msg from being explicitly freed after it has already been handed off to send_ctx when a flush operation fails, avoiding an invalid free or double-free while preserving the remaining cleanup steps such as restoring send credits.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is visible in the snippet, especially in smb_direct_post_send_data() and smb_direct_flush_send_list(). In smb_direct_post_send_data(), the error path still does `smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, msg);` after `smb_direct_flush_send_list(t, send_ctx);` has been called: `ret = smb_direct_flush_send_list(t, send_ctx); if (ret) goto err; ... err: smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, msg);`. The root cause says ownership of `msg` was moved into `send_ctx` by post_sendmsg, so after flushing the send list, freeing `msg` again is a double free. The diff also shows that `smb_direct_flush_send_list()` frees every entry in `send_ctx->msg_list` via `list_for_each_entry_safe(first, last, &send_ctx->msg_list, sibling_list) { smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, first); }`, confirming that the flushed list owns and frees queued send messages. This commit only changes the helper signatures from taking `struct smb_direct_transport *t` to `struct smbdirect_socket *sc`; it does not add any ownership reset, nulling, conditional free, or other protection in smb_direct_post_send_data(). Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet included.

The vulnerable construct is present after `ret = post_sendmsg(sc, send_ctx, msg);` followed by `if (ret) goto err;`. The code then has a second path for local `_send_ctx`: `ret = smb_direct_flush_send_list(sc, send_ctx, true); if (ret) goto err;`. bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the relevant ownership-transfer path: `post_sendmsg()`, `smb_direct_flush_send_list()`, and the error handling in `smb_direct_post_send_data()`. In `post_sendmsg()`, when `send_ctx` is used, the message is linked into `send_ctx->msg_list` via `list_add_tail(&msg->sibling_list, &send_ctx->msg_list);` and the function returns 0, which means ownership of `msg` has effectively moved into the send context. In `smb_direct_flush_send_list()`, on failure of `ib_post_send()`, the function frees every queued message with `list_for_each_entry_safe(first, last, &send_ctx->msg_list, sibling_list) { smb_direct_free_sendmsg(t, first); }`. However, in `smb_direct_post_send_data()`, after `ret = post_sendmsg(t, send_ctx, msg); if (ret) goto err;`, the `err:` path still does `if (msg) smb_direct_free_sendmsg(t, msg);`. There is no clearing of `msg` after successful `post_sendmsg()`, so if a later failure causes `smb_direct_flush_send_list()` to free the queued messages, the local `msg` variable can still point to one of those already-freed send messages and be freed again on the common error path. That matches the stated root cause: the code continues treating sendmsg ownership as local after `post_sendmsg()` moved it into `send_ctx`. No fix is present here such as nulling `msg` after successful enqueue/transfer or otherwise preventing the second free.
